# Styling

`style` is an explicit, **non-web** prop on every widget. GTK styling is NOT web CSS: there is no `flex`, `grid`, `position`, `display`, or `justifyContent`. Layout comes from container widgets (`<box>`/`<grid>`), not from `style`. Unknown keys are rejected at the React renderer with a fix-it message and defensively rejected host-side.

## Valid keys

| Key | Shape | Compiles to |
|---|---|---|
| `background` | color | GTK CSS (`background-color`) |
| `color` | color | GTK CSS (`color`) |
| `font` | object (fontSize, fontWeight, fontFamily) | GTK CSS (`nested`) |
| `padding` | spacing | GTK CSS (`padding`) |
| `margin` | spacing | GTK widget property (not CSS) |
| `hexpand` | bool | GTK widget property (not CSS) |
| `vexpand` | bool | GTK widget property (not CSS) |
| `halign` | enum | GTK widget property (not CSS) |
| `valign` | enum | GTK widget property (not CSS) |
| `border` | object (borderWidth, borderColor, borderRadius) | GTK CSS (`nested`) |

## Why `margin` differs from `padding`

GTK widget **margins are widget properties** (`gtk_widget_set_margin_*`), not CSS — so `margin` compiles to `setMarginStart/End/Top/Bottom`. `padding` IS a GTK CSS property and stays in the generated `.nd-<id>` CSS block, alongside colors, fonts, and borders. (M5c-D2.)
